newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols soft, dlr/yen vols seesaw.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols soft, dlr/yen vols seesaw.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options were a touch softer in thin U.S. business, even though the dollar fell below 1.82 marks and extended its sharp retracement from last week's highs, traders said.
Front-end dollar/yen volatilities, on the other hand, seesawed as the dollar tumbled below 117 yen after rallying overnight toward 119 yen.
Dollar/mark volatilities from the one-month to three-month area was pegged at around 10.8/11.1 percent in early afternoon U.S., 0.1 to 0.2 point lower on the day.
"They do get a little bid while spot is moving but just settle down around here once spot stops moving," a dealer at a Japanese bank in New York said.
The dollar flirted with the 1.82-mark level for most of the U.S. session after selling off earlier to a low of 1.8155 marks due in part to a drop in U.S. stock and bond prices.
Although the retracement from the August 6 high of 1.8913 marks has been steep, it has yet to stoke fears of a meltdown.
"For the time being, in the immediate vicinity of where we're trading, there's still more fear on the (dollar's) upside," Alan Revercomb, options strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc.
Risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, remained at par to slightly skewed for mark puts.
By contrast, dollar/yen volatilities were choppy.
Shorter-dated volatilities spiked up overnight after huge buying of 118.10 yen yen puts expiring Monday and the dollar's climb to a 118.70 yen high in thin trading.
"What that creates is a lot of nervousness," Revercomb said, noting that many bank dealers took on negative gamma exposures in those strike prices as a result of the trade.
"Dealers have pretty uncomfortable positions with a higher dollar," he said.

Negative gamma positions benefit from time decay but are vulnerable to spot market movements. Because their delta would increase as the dollar falls and decrease as the dollar rises, dealers would have to buy dollars at highs and sell at lows.
"Delta-hedging by negative gamma option traders in this thin market might be one reason the dollar has been so choppy in both directions," the Japanese bank dealer noted.

Still, as the dollar fell to a low of 116.85 yen, dealers were quick to deflate the front end. One-month dollar/yen was at 11.8/12.1 percent in the early afternoon, down from early highs around 12.4 but up from around 11 late on Thursday.
One-year was more stable at higher levels at 12.2/12.4 percent against Thursday's 11.4/11.6.
The big Monday-expiry buying was said to have been linked to an exotic option that had a trigger at 118.10 yen and was thus wiped out by the dollar's rally.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal flipped in favor of yen puts and was as wide as 0.4/0.8 point before coming back in toward neutral.
A September 26-expiry 25-delta yen call buying against at-the-money selling that totaled nearly $1 billion helped push back the risk reversal.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
